reading: TV presenter Alison Hammond experienced a health scare during a live broadcast last week.
She quickly left the programme, clutching her chest, and went to the hospital for a check-up.
Doctors confirmed she had suffered a panic attack, not a heart attack, which she described as "probably one of the most scariest things I've ever been through".
Hammond explained she couldn't catch her breath and genuinely believed she was having a heart attack on air.
She added that the experience felt very real, like "a wave" of adrenaline overwhelming her body.
Upon returning to her weekly slot, she expressed gratitude, saying the event had given her a new perspective on life.
She even compared the feeling to entering a place, like the "Upside Down world" from the TV show Stranger Things.
She admitted she was anxious about returning to the show, fearing that if she didn't come back immediately, she might never do so.
Panic attacks are an extreme anxiety response that can cause both physical and mental symptoms.
These attacks can mimic heart attack symptoms such as chest pain, but heart attack pain often spreads to the arm or jaw.
To manage a panic attack, experts advise focusing on the present moment, one's surroundings, and steadying one's breathing.
